review_notes:
I read all of Basic.lean (lines 1–106). I also read the uses in IwasawaModules/PseudoIsomorphism/LinearMap.lean and searched the repo for other uses of IsPseudoNull. The file has no @[simp] attributes. IsPseudoNull is an @[expose] def with no simp-unfolding lemma. The one place the file simplifies, isPseudoNull_iff_localizedModule_subsingleton, uses `simp only [IsPseudoNull, Module.notMem_support_iff]`. That is a local, controlled unfolding with no competing rules. Downstream code in LinearMap.lean uses these results through explicit `rw [...]` and `exact`, not through simp. I considered three candidates and rejected each:
- Marking of_subsingleton as simp or as an instance. Its only downstream uses (LinearMap.lean lines 96 and 98) are explicit `exact` calls after `rw`, so simp would not help them.
- Marking the iff lemmas (isPseudoNull_iff_of_exact, isPseudoNull_iff_submodule_quotient) as simp. They need explicit maps or arguments, and the submodule/quotient form would rewrite a module into a more complex pair of statements, which makes it unsuitable as a simp rule.
- Marking LinearEquiv.isPseudoNull_iff as simp. It is a non-canonical transport lemma with no stated normal form.
I found no concrete simp-interface defect. I did not run Lean, so I can't rule out simp-behaviour problems that only show up when simp is run.
